# Current State in the Company {#sec-current-state}


## Internal Survey

An internal survey conducted between August and September 2026 received 57 responses. It was distributed through four Google Chat rooms: two team rooms and two rooms focused on AI users and AI products. Several employees were also contacted directly. This sampling favors employees with high AI interest and adoption. The results therefore describe an AI-active subgroup rather than company-wide usage.

Respondents reported one first-choice configuration and up to three additional configurations used at least weekly. The two Claude Code answer labels were merged. Adoption rates count each respondent once per harness or model; configuration analyses count each distinct respondent--harness--model pair once. "Other" and automatically selected models are excluded where a named model or provider is required.

The model list was fixed when the survey was published and was not updated for later releases. Models released afterwards, including DeepSeek V4.1 Flash and GLM-5.3-Flash, were therefore not available as named choices. Their adoption may consequently be understated in the survey.

```{python}
#| include: false

from scripts.figures import (
    plot_grouped_bar,
    plot_pie,
    plot_pie_comparison,
    plot_stacked_percent,
)
from scripts.survey_analysis import (
    configuration_usage,
    harness_tier_distribution,
    harness_usage,
    load_model_tiers,
    load_survey,
    model_usage,
    provider_diversification,
    reported_cost_distribution,
    role_tier_distribution,
)

survey = load_survey("data/company-survey.csv")
model_tiers = load_model_tiers("data/model-cost-tiers.csv")
```

## Harness-Model Configurations

The combined configurations show a clear Claude-centered pattern. Claude Code with Claude Opus 5 was the most common primary configuration, selected by 18 of 57 respondents (31.6%), and appeared in 24 weekly workflows (42.1%). Claude Code with Claude Sonnet 5 appeared in 15 workflows (26.3%), followed by Claude Code with Claude Sonnet 4.6 in 11 (19.3%). @fig-survey-configuration-usage shows the eight most common named configurations.

```{python}
#| label: fig-survey-configuration-usage
#| fig-cap: "Most common named harness--model configurations among survey respondents (n = 57)."
#| fig-alt: "Horizontal grouped bar chart of the eight most common named harness-model configurations. Claude Code with Claude Opus 5 is the most common primary and weekly configuration, followed by Claude Code with Claude Sonnet 5 and Claude Sonnet 4.6."
#| fig-width: 7.2
#| fig-format: svg
#| fig-height: 5.2

plot_grouped_bar(
    configuration_usage(survey, limit=8),
    category_col="configuration",
    value_cols=["Primary %", "Any weekly use %"],
    series_labels=["Primary configuration", "Any weekly use"],
    horizontal=True,
    x_label="Respondents (%)",
    percentage_axis=True,
)
```

*Source: own analysis of the internal survey. Unnamed configurations are omitted.*

## Harness Usage

Claude Code was the first-choice harness for 41 of 57 respondents (71.9%) and was used weekly by 52 (91.2%). OpenCode ranked second with 8 first-choice responses (14.0%) and 15 weekly users (26.3%). Codex and GitHub Copilot each had 9 weekly users (15.8%); Pi had 5 (8.8%). @fig-survey-harness-usage compares first-choice and weekly use.

```{python}
#| label: fig-survey-harness-usage
#| fig-cap: "First-choice and weekly harness usage among survey respondents (n = 57)."
#| fig-alt: "Horizontal grouped bar chart comparing first-choice harness usage with any reported weekly use. Claude Code is substantially higher than every alternative in both measures."
#| fig-width: 7.2
#| fig-format: svg
#| fig-height: 4.5

plot_grouped_bar(
    harness_usage(survey),
    category_col="harness",
    value_cols=["First choice %", "Any weekly use %"],
    series_labels=["First choice", "Any weekly use"],
    horizontal=True,
    x_label="Respondents (%)",
    percentage_axis=True,
)
```

*Source: own analysis of the internal survey.*

Multiple setups were common. A total of 42 respondents (73.7%) reported at least one additional setup or model used weekly, and 32 (56.1%) used two or more harnesses. Claude Code with OpenCode was the most common multi-harness combination, reported by 12 respondents.

Alternative harnesses mostly complemented Claude Code. Among weekly users, 12 of 15 OpenCode users and 8 of 9 Codex users also used Claude Code. The same applied to all 9 GitHub Copilot users, all 7 Antigravity users, and all 5 Pi users.

## Model Usage

Anthropic models were similarly concentrated. An Anthropic model was primary for 42 respondents (73.7%), and 51 (89.5%) used at least one named Anthropic model weekly.

Claude Opus 5 was the most common primary model with 20 respondents (35.1%), followed by Claude Sonnet 4.6 with 11 (19.3%) and Claude Sonnet 5 with 8 (14.0%). Weekly use was 27 respondents for Opus 5 (47.4%), 15 for Sonnet 5 (26.3%), and 13 for Sonnet 4.6 (22.8%). @fig-survey-model-usage shows the full distribution of named models.

```{python}
#| label: fig-survey-model-usage
#| fig-cap: "Primary and weekly usage of named models among survey respondents (n = 57)."
#| fig-alt: "Horizontal grouped bar chart of named models. Claude Opus 5 has the highest primary and weekly adoption, followed by Claude Sonnet 5 and Claude Sonnet 4.6."
#| fig-width: 7.2
#| fig-format: svg
#| fig-height: 6.5

plot_grouped_bar(
    model_usage(survey),
    category_col="model",
    value_cols=["Primary %", "Any weekly use %"],
    series_labels=["Primary model", "Any weekly use"],
    horizontal=True,
    x_label="Respondents (%)",
    percentage_axis=True,
)
```

*Source: own analysis of the internal survey. Unnamed models are omitted.*

Non-Anthropic models were common but rarely used alone. Of the 57 respondents, 27 (47.4%) reported only named Anthropic models, 24 (42.1%) combined Anthropic with another provider, and 5 (8.8%) used only non-Anthropic models. One response could not be classified by provider. @fig-survey-provider-diversification shows the resulting provider-use groups.

```{python}
#| label: fig-survey-provider-diversification
#| fig-cap: "Anthropic-only and alternative-provider model use among survey respondents."
#| fig-alt: "Pie chart showing 47.4 percent Anthropic-only use, 42.1 percent combined Anthropic and alternative-provider use, 8.8 percent alternative-provider-only use, and one unclassified response."
#| fig-width: 6.5
#| fig-format: svg
#| fig-height: 4.4

provider_groups = provider_diversification(survey)
_ = plot_pie(
    provider_groups,
    category_col="category",
    value_col="respondents",
    min_label_percent=3.0,
)
```

*Source: own analysis of the internal survey. One respondent (1.8%) could not be classified because no named model provider could be identified.*

Among these respondents, alternative providers therefore mostly complement rather than replace Anthropic.

## Model Cost Tiers

Named models were grouped by the average cost per task of their best-listed DeepSWE v1.1 configuration [@deepsweLeaderboard2026]. Costs below USD 2 are classified as low, USD 2 to below USD 5 as medium, and USD 5 or more as high. @tbl-model-cost-tiers summarizes the resulting tiers. Unnamed models remain excluded.

| Tier | DeepSWE criterion | Models |
|---|---|---|
| High cost | USD 5 or more per task | Claude Opus 5; Claude Sonnet 5; Claude Sonnet 4.6; Claude Fable 5; Claude Opus 4.8; GPT-5.6 Sol |
| Medium cost | USD 2 to below USD 5 per task | GPT-5.6 Terra; Gemini 3.1 Pro; Gemini 3.6 Flash; Kimi K3; Claude Haiku 4.5 |
| Low cost | Below USD 2 per task | GPT-5.6 Luna; DeepSeek V4 Flash 0731; MiniMax M3 |

: Model cost tiers used for the survey analysis. {#tbl-model-cost-tiers}

Claude Haiku 4.5 and MiniMax M3 have no comparable DeepSWE v1.1 result and are therefore pricing-based additions rather than DeepSWE-derived classifications. Claude Haiku 4.5 is assigned to the medium-cost tier from its official pricing of USD 1/M input and USD 5/M output tokens [@anthropicHaiku45Pricing2025]. MiniMax M3 is assigned to the low-cost tier from its official API token pricing [@minimaxM3Pricing2026].

Model cost differs by harness. In @fig-survey-harness-cost-tier, 55 of 57 classifiable Claude Code configurations (96.5%) use high-cost models and 2 (3.5%) use medium-cost models. OpenCode spans all three tiers: 40.0% high, 33.3% medium, and 26.7% low cost. Three of the four classifiable Pi configurations are low cost. Small samples for less common harnesses limit these comparisons.

```{python}
#| label: fig-survey-harness-cost-tier
#| fig-cap: "Model cost-tier distribution by harness for classifiable weekly configurations."
#| fig-alt: "One-hundred-percent stacked horizontal bars by harness. Claude Code is 96.5 percent high cost and 3.5 percent medium cost after including Claude Haiku 4.5 in the medium tier. OpenCode spans all three tiers, and Pi is mostly low cost. Each harness label includes its number of classifiable configurations."
#| fig-width: 7.2
#| fig-format: svg
#| fig-height: 4.4

harness_tiers = harness_tier_distribution(
    survey,
    model_tiers,
    ["Claude Code", "OpenCode", "Codex", "GitHub Copilot", "Antigravity", "Pi"],
)
plot_stacked_percent(
    harness_tiers,
    category_col="harness_label",
    value_cols=["High cost", "Medium cost", "Low cost"],
    horizontal=True,
    min_label_percent=3.0,
)
```

*Source: own analysis of the internal survey. Tier boundaries use DeepSWE v1.1 average cost per task [@deepsweLeaderboard2026], with pricing-based fallbacks for MiniMax M3 [@minimaxM3Pricing2026] and Claude Haiku 4.5 [@anthropicHaiku45Pricing2025].*

Cost tier also differs between primary and secondary configurations. High-cost models account for 81.1% of classifiable primary configurations and 55.1% of secondary configurations. Medium-cost models rise from 7.5% of primary to 34.7% of secondary configurations, while low-cost models account for 11.3% and 10.2%, respectively (@fig-survey-role-cost-tier).

```{python}
#| label: fig-survey-role-cost-tier
#| fig-cap: "Model cost-tier distribution for primary and secondary survey configurations."
#| fig-alt: "Two pie charts comparing primary and secondary configurations. Primary configurations are 81.1 percent high, 7.5 percent medium, and 11.3 percent low cost. Secondary configurations are 55.1 percent high, 34.7 percent medium, and 10.2 percent low cost after including Claude Haiku 4.5 in the medium tier."
#| fig-width: 6.8
#| fig-format: svg
#| fig-height: 3.6

role_tiers = role_tier_distribution(survey, model_tiers)
_ = plot_pie_comparison(
    role_tiers,
    category_col="role_label",
    value_cols=["High cost", "Medium cost", "Low cost"],
    min_label_percent=3.0,
)
```

*Source: own analysis of the internal survey. Primary and secondary pies contain 53 and 49 classifiable configurations, respectively.*

The respondent-level data show the same association. Of the 17 respondents using at least one medium-cost model, 13 (76.5%) used multiple named providers and 13 (76.5%) used multiple harnesses. Among the 40 respondents without a medium-cost model, 11 (27.5%) used multiple named providers. This exploratory result suggests that medium-cost models are more common in diversified workflows.

## Reported Cost

Monthly coding-agent cost was reported in categories rather than exact amounts. Of the 57 responses, 33 gave a monetary range, 15 selected a flat-rate subscription, 8 selected "I don't know", and 1 was blank. Among the 33 monetary responses, 22 (66.7%) reported at least EUR 100 per month. @fig-survey-reported-cost keeps the original categories instead of converting ranges to estimated values.

```{python}
#| label: fig-survey-reported-cost
#| fig-cap: "Reported monthly AI coding-agent cost categories among survey respondents (n = 57)."
#| fig-alt: "Pie chart of the original monthly cost response categories. Flat-rate subscription is the most common category, followed by EUR 100-199, EUR 20-49, EUR 200-499, and unknown cost."
#| fig-width: 7.0
#| fig-format: svg
#| fig-height: 5.0

_ = plot_pie(
    reported_cost_distribution(survey),
    category_col="category",
    value_col="respondents",
    min_label_percent=3.0,
)
```

*Source: own analysis of the internal survey.*

The cost categories are not directly comparable as continuous values, so no average expenditure is derived.

Overall, the sample shows a strong Claude Code and Anthropic baseline with alternatives layered around it. High-cost models dominate primary configurations, while medium-cost models are more common in secondary and diversified setups. Because the survey targeted AI-active groups, these results characterize advanced internal users rather than company-wide adoption.
